_meta.author: content pack (doc 47), 10 Oct 2026: designed; each card's basis names what it rests on
_meta.note: window = [from, to] quarters (equal for a fixed-quarter card). reading_sign: the scarcity-exposure sign each choice logs, keyed by choice label (README); a choice not listed logs 0; 'raise_rule' = the M41 raise rule (the sign of the next scored move, -1 if none follows). Interrupt cards fire when their condition holds inside the window (README, 'Card firing').

event_cards.title: Act V Opens
event_cards.body: The plants you backed a decade ago are starting to switch on, and the grid queue runs years long. Nobody can tell you what kind of megawatt the late 2030s will pay for. The futures ahead are scenarios, not forecasts: read the signals.

event_cards.title: The Seventh Halving
event_cards.body: The block subsidy halves to 0.390625 coins. Miners that barely covered their power bill now lose money every hour they run, unless someone pays them to switch off.

choices.label: Enrol the miners as flexible load

event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q9: block 1,470,000 [A]; quarter 2036Q1 [D]; market files halve the subsidy in 2036Q1

event_cards.title: The Credit Cliff
event_cards.body: The federal clean-power credit is gone for any project that starts construction from 2036. Plants that started by 2033 keep theirs; everything new competes on its own numbers.
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q8: OBBB phase-down, full credit to 2033 starts, 75% 2034, 50% 2035, none after [A/B]

event_cards.title: The Licensing Clock
event_cards.body: The reactor regulator commits to decisions within eighteen months, and its new rulebook is in force. Every small reactor still waiting for a licence moves up two quarters.
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q8: the 2025 nuclear orders' 18-month target, Part 53 in force Apr 2026 [A/B]; doc 43 §0.4 (−2 q, every future)

event_cards.title: Quantum-Safe by Law
event_cards.body: The deadline for retiring pre-quantum signatures has passed for government systems. Bitcoin's developers are still arguing over how to move old coins to new keys.

choices.label: Move the treasury's coins to fresh wallets

event_cards.basis: Doc 40 §D6, doc 45 §Q9: NIST IR 8547 disallows RSA/ECDSA after 2035 [A/B]; cost designed

event_cards.title: The Roadmap Runs Out
event_cards.body: The chipmakers' published roadmaps end with this year's generation. Nobody has announced what comes after, so the GPUs you buy now may be the last named class for a while.
event_cards.basis: Doc 40 §D2: imec's roadmap horizon ~2038 [C]; doc 43 §19 ("no announced generation after 2038")

event_cards.title: Plant Trip
event_cards.body: One of your operating plants trips offline: a pump seal, then a cautious restart. The crew can be back in a week, or faster if you pay for weekend shifts and a spare.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §14.2 (plant trip interrupt); designed: once per operating plant per 8 quarters at most, 15%/q chance (README)

event_cards.title: Venture Cash Call
event_cards.body: A venture you hold a stake in has reached its next build tranche and the overrun is due. Pay your share, let your stake dilute, or walk away.
event_cards.basis: Doc 38 §5.1 (tranches); docs/energy-content (unanswered: dilute); the card fires when a carried draw calls

event_cards.title: Transformer Delay
event_cards.body: The substation transformer for one of your queue positions is late from the factory. Expediting a unit from another project costs money; waiting costs a quarter.
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q8: large transformers 128-144 weeks, shortage through ~2030 [C]; $20/kW designed

event_cards.title: The Eighth Halving
event_cards.body: The subsidy halves again, to 0.1953125 coins. Thirty-one years after the first block, a coin's worth of mining takes eight halvings of patience.
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q9: block 1,680,000 [A]; quarter 2040Q1 [D]

event_cards.title: The Buyers Arrive
event_cards.body: Strategic buyers and funds are asking for your data room. You can sell the company, sell the plants and keep the platform, or hold. The bid is known; what comes after 2040 is not.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §15.2 (the founder's exit, 2040Q3-Q4)

event_cards.title: Five Years and Counting
event_cards.body: The study for your next 100 MW comes back: twenty quarters to connect, and a bill to stay in line. Two brokers call the same week asking whether your free megawatts are for sale.

choices.label: Ask for a bid on one site

event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q3: PJM 40-month average, data-centre zones 36-48 months [C]; LBNL 5.1-year median [A]

event_cards.title: Dozens of Reactors
event_cards.body: Ironvale Power and two utilities announce orderbooks for two dozen small reactors, and a fast-track licensing order follows. Commentators say firm power will be plentiful by the early 2040s.

choices.label: Lock your tenants in for ten years at today's rate

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.4: the SMR wave decoy; 2026 orderbooks disclose no funding, Doicești FID without funding [A/B]

event_cards.title: At the Cap, Again
event_cards.body: The capacity auction clears at the cap in every zone, and the uncapped price is the highest on record. Utilities start asking large loads to bring their own power.

choices.label: Reserve a turbine slot for on-site gas

event_cards.basis: Doc 40 §D8: PJM 2028/29 uncapped 71% above the cap [C]; turbine reservation designed

event_cards.title: The Five-Year Line
event_cards.body: Every big region's grid queue passes five years for a firm connection, and the reform bills stall in committee. Whoever already holds firm megawatts sets the price.

choices.label: Spend goodwill to defend your positions

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V1); doc 45 §Q3 waits; market_v_v1 scarcity 1.10 at 2037Q4

event_cards.title: A Fund Comes Calling
event_cards.body: Hollowfield Infrastructure wants one of your operating plant stakes for its long-dated fund and offers above the market's index. The partner says the bid is good for one quarter.
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q1: Atlantica take-private at +18.9% to undisturbed [B]; Goldendale bought by a fund [B]

event_cards.title: Premium for a Place in Line
event_cards.body: Carrack Compute pays a record premium for a half-built campus that holds a queue position, then calls you with an offer for one of yours. The premium per kilowatt has doubled since 2036.

choices.label: Sell a site with its position

event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q3: positions transfer only with the facility [A/C]; powered land ~$300K/MW [C]; V1 premium path designed

event_cards.title: A Block Reaches Its End
event_cards.body: One of your orbital blocks reaches the end of its design life. Launch is a little cheaper than in 2036, but bringing the tenant home needs ground megawatts, the scarcest thing you own.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §9.1 (replacement cycle); fires at each block's end of life (2031-35 launches)

event_cards.title: Firm Megawatts Set the Price
event_cards.body: Merchant power is up a quarter on 2036 and every renewal reopens at scarcity prices. Plants that stayed merchant are earning more each quarter than they did the one before.

choices.label: Contract half your plant output for 15 years

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V1 rewards firm plants held merchant or re-contracted late); market_v_v1 merchant power +25%

event_cards.title: A Rule That Moves
event_cards.body: The federal regulator approves the first grid operator's large-load filing. Your lawyers say a real fast lane could open within a year for loads that accept curtailment.

choices.label: Pay to model your sites' flexibility

event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q3: FERC's June 2026 show-cause orders to all six RTOs [A/B]; SPP's large-load process [A]

event_cards.title: Firm Power for Everyone
event_cards.body: Ironvale Power unveils a twenty-reactor orderbook with three utilities, and the headlines say firm power will be cheap by 2042. Two of your tenants ask whether they should wait to renew.

choices.label: Lock your tenants in for ten years at today's rate

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.4: the SMR wave decoy [A/B for its basis]

event_cards.title: The Curtailment Manager Works
event_cards.body: ERCOT's curtailment manager clears its trial: loads on 24-hour notice can be cut for a few hours at a time without tripping the grid. Two more grid operators file similar rules.

choices.label: Enrol a test hall as flexible

event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q3: Texas SB6 24-hour notice [B]; ERCOT's Large Load Curtailment Manager [A]; Duke 0.5% ≈ 177 h [C]

event_cards.title: The Flexible Lane Opens
event_cards.body: The first large-load fast lane goes live: loads that accept up to 180 hours of curtailment a year connect in under two years. Firm power stops being the only way in.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §0.4: fast lane 4-8 q, ≤180 h/yr, −0.5% output, 24-h notice [B/C]; the 1-3 year connection is [D]

event_cards.title: An Upgrade Bill Nobody Needs
event_cards.body: A study names the network upgrade bill for one of your firm requests. The fast lane would connect the same hall sooner, if your tenant accepts a few hours of curtailment a year.

choices.label: Pay the bill and keep the position
Withdraw and apply for the fast lane

event_cards.default: Pay the bill and keep the position
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q3: the study names the bill; pay to stay or withdraw [A]

event_cards.title: Flexible Capacity Bids In
event_cards.body: Curtailable load now counts as supply in the capacity auction. Your miners and battery-backed halls could bid, and the capacity price you pay elsewhere is falling.
event_cards.basis: Doc 40 §D7 and doc 45 §Q3 (flexible load services in the show-cause orders) [A/B]; payment designed (README)

event_cards.title: A Block Reaches Its End
event_cards.body: One of your orbital blocks reaches the end of its design life. With the fast lane open, a ground hall could take the tenant within a year, if it accepts some curtailment.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §9.1 (replacement cycle)

event_cards.title: Flexibility Pays
event_cards.body: Half the new data-centre load of the last two years connected through the fast lane. Firm power still sells, but the premium for it is the smallest since the early 2030s.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V2 rewards flexible loads and co-location); market_v_v2

event_cards.title: A Record Auction
event_cards.body: The capacity auction clears at the cap after a wave of old plant retirements, and the uncapped price is the highest ever. Traders call it the squeeze everyone has been waiting for.

choices.label: Buy a queue-holding site before prices run

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.4: V3's record-auction decoy (designed); PJM 2028/29 uncapped price far above the cap as its shape [C]

event_cards.title: Idle GPUs
event_cards.body: Spot GPU rates slide on idle capacity, and a lab hands back 20 MW a year early. Its finance team asks whether you would extend the rest of its lease at a discount.

choices.label: Offer a long extension at 5% off

event_cards.basis: Doc 40 §D8 (V3 indicators: GPU rental prices sliding) [C]; designed

event_cards.title: Withdrawals Climb
event_cards.body: Queue withdrawals jump as speculative sites give back their positions, and your own study bill comes in lower than expected. The network has headroom again in two zones.

choices.label: Sell a site with its position while premiums hold

event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q3: 65-80% of PJM 2018-20 capacity withdrew [C]; LBNL 75% withdrew [A]

event_cards.title: The Capex Pause
event_cards.body: Two of the largest AI buyers cut next year's data-centre spending and walk away from queued sites. Speculative requests start withdrawing by the hundred.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V3): IEA low case ~700 TWh by 2035 [C]; plateau [D]

event_cards.title: Merchant Prices Fall
event_cards.body: Merchant power is down nearly a third on a year ago and capacity clears at half the cap. Buyers who would not sign last year now want fifteen-year contracts at today's lower price.

choices.label: Contract 80% of plant output at market minus 10%

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V3 merchant −30%, capacity −50%); doc 40 §Q6: ERCOT batteries $192 → $55/kW-yr as the saturation precedent [C]

event_cards.title: A Discounted Next Unit
event_cards.body: The developer of your plant offers the next unit at a discount to keep its crews together. It would reach first power after 2040, into a market that no longer needs it.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §7.4 (follow-on units, a +1 move) and §13 (late follow-on units punished in V3)

event_cards.title: A Block Reaches Its End
event_cards.body: One of your orbital blocks reaches the end of its design life. Ground halls are emptying and cheap; orbit is no cheaper than it was.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §9.1 (replacement cycle)

event_cards.title: Lenders Tighten
event_cards.body: Hollowfield Infrastructure's lenders warn that merchant plants across the market are breaking their coverage tests. Any plant of yours below 1.15 keeps its cash inside the project until it recovers.
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q2: lock-up below DSCR 1.15, restructure after 4 q below 1.0, step-in after 8 [C]

event_cards.title: Twenty Flights, One Booster
event_cards.body: Carrack Heavy flies the same booster for the twentieth time and quotes third-party seats for 2038 well under list. Two of your orbital tenants ask about the next generation of satellites.
event_cards.basis: Doc 40 §D3: launch below $200/kg needs ~180 heavy launches a year [C]

event_cards.title: A Reactor in Every Region
event_cards.body: Ironvale Power and two utilities announce a twenty-reactor orderbook and promise abundant firm power by the mid-2040s. A broker offers to buy one of your sites now, before the supply arrives.

choices.label: Sell a site while ground is dear

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.4: the SMR wave decoy [A/B for its basis]

event_cards.title: Northgate Matches the Price
event_cards.body: Northgate matches Carrack's third-party price for the first time, and lighter satellites are due within months. Orbital compute builders start booking a year of launches at a time.
event_cards.basis: Doc 40 §D3: Forethought ~$100/kg competitive [C]; doc 33 (Northgate, the second launcher)

event_cards.title: Launch Breaks $200
event_cards.body: Carrack Heavy posts a third-party price under $200 a kilogram and a weekly flight rate. Orbit starts taking the marginal gigawatt, and the space multiple jumps.

choices.label: Raise equity at the space multiple

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V4): Google's learning-curve conditional, SemiAnalysis ~2040 parity [C]

event_cards.title: A Block Reaches Its End
event_cards.body: One of your orbital blocks reaches the end of its design life. Replacement launch and satellites cost less than half what they did in 2036, and tenants are queuing for capacity.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §9.1 (replacement cycle; V4 rewards replacers)

event_cards.title: Ground Rents Soften
event_cards.body: Inference tenants are moving new load to orbit, and your renewal offers come back lower than last year's. Two tenants would sign for ten years if you hold today's rate.

choices.label: Lock both tenants in for ten years

event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V4: ground prices soften late); market_v_v4 scarcity 0.95 → 0.90

event_cards.title: A Fund Prices the Softening
event_cards.body: Hollowfield Infrastructure bids for one of your plant stakes, a little under its index: it says ground power is past its peak. The bid is good for one quarter.
event_cards.basis: Doc 45 §Q1 (fund bids at an index) [B/C]; market_v_v4 infra_bid_index 0.95

event_cards.title: The Marginal Gigawatt Goes Up
event_cards.body: More new AI capacity was launched this year than was connected to the ground grid. The companies that kept replacing their satellites are booking the rents.
event_cards.basis: Doc 43 §6.2 (V4 rewards orbit replacers)
